speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities in detail, including when it started, how it looks, and if you have had any recent exposure to new products or foods.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: That 5-month duration suggests a chronic condition; does the rash appear in specific patterns like lines or rings, or does it look like isolated bumps? Additionally, have you noticed if the itch is significantly worse at night?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Prurigo Simplex (Prurigo Simplex of the arms). The chronic nature (5 months), bilateral distribution on the extremities, intense pruritus, and absence of systemic symptoms or recent triggers strongly support this diagnosis over acute allergic reactions or scabies.
